propositions: The byte-equivalence oracle executes a copied _legacy_convert subprocess for all 884 prepared corpus units, duplicating 884 real Pandoc invocations unnecessarily and adding 32.9979s runtime.

The copied legacy oracle reads the same mutable _PANDOC_TO production constant as the oracle being tested, causing both sides to drift identically when the constant changes, making the oracle fail to detect production format mutations.
The single-platform provenance schema (macOS arm64 SHA-256) is treated as platform-independent in CI, causing rejection on Ubuntu x86_64 gates despite identical Pandoc 3.6.1 version.

Replacing the copied _legacy_convert subprocess call with immutable golden-output fixtures removes the 884 duplicate Pandoc subprocesses while preserving all 884 real production _convert/Pandoc calls and maintaining independent mutation detection.
